verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's left the porch light burning
though it's well past dawn now —
still, I don't go turn it off.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Coffee gone cold in the cup by the window —
I meant to drink it hours ago,
meant a lot of things.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A crow lands on the fence, considers,
then leaves without a word —
some visits are just weather passing through.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in the next room —
nobody moves to pour it,
we're listening to something else entirely.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a screen door slaps shut twice —
once for the leaving,
once for whoever forgot something.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light stays on past midnight —
not for anyone coming home,
just old habit keeping watch.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's dog stops barking mid-bark —
some smaller silence
swallowed whatever it heard first.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Frost writes its name on the window overnight —
by noon it's just water,
already forgetting the shape it made.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it was ever cold —
steam rising
like it never happened.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone else's coat still on the hook —
the hallway hasn't noticed
it's been months since anyone left it there.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light left on through breakfast —
somebody's small apology
still burning in the daylight.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Crumbs on the table, nobody's chair pushed in —
the morning
already practicing being alone.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mailbox flag still up from Tuesday —
nobody's news
waiting to be wanted.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A cup rinsed but not put away —
even the sink
learns to leave something unfinished.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits by the door anyway —
some habits
never read the calendar.
